title: Definition
body_md: An {\it involution} on a $k$-algebra $A$ is a $k$-algebra homomorphism $\sigma\,:\, A \rightarrow A^{\mathrm{op}}$ such that $\sigma^{\mathrm{op}} \circ \sigma\,=\,{\rm{Id}}$. Equivalently, $\sigma$ is a square identity $k$-linear map from $A$ to itself such that for all $a,b \,\in\,A$, $\sigma(ab)\,=\,\sigma(b)\sigma(a)$.

title: Proof
body_md:
We claim that the inverse of $\mathcal{M}_n(\mbox{--})$ is the functor
 
\begin{equation} \la{Ginv} (\mbox{--})^{\mathcal{M}_n(k)} \,:\, \mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_{\mathcal{M}_n(k)} \rightarrow
\mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_k\,,\,\,\,\, A \mapsto A^{\mathcal{M}_n(k)} \,\text{.}\end{equation}
 
Here, $A^{\mathcal{M}_n(k)}$ denotes the DG subalgebra of elements in $A$ commuting with all elements in $\mathcal{M}_n(k)$. Observe that $(\mbox{--})^{\mathcal{M}_n(k)}$ is well defined: if $A \in \mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_{\mathcal{M}_n(k)}$ with involution $\sigma$, $\sigma$ induces
an involution on $A^{\mathcal{M}_n(k)}$: indeed, if $[m\,,\,a]=0$ for all $m \in \mathcal{M}_n(k)$, $[\sigma(m)\,,\,\sigma(a)]\,=\,-\sigma([m\,,\,a])=0$
for all $m \in \mathcal{M}_n(k)$. Hence, $a \in A^{\mathcal{M}_n(k)}$ implies that $\sigma(a) \in A^{\mathcal{M}_n(k)}$. 
 
That $(\mbox{--})^{\mathcal{M}_n(k)} \circ \mathcal{M}_n(\mbox{--}) \,=\,{\rm{Id}}$
amounts to checking that $(\mathcal{M}_n(B))^{\mathcal{M}_n(k)} \cong B$. The left hand side is n by n matrices $b=\Sigma b_{ij}$ with coefficients in $B$ such that $[b,e_{k\ell}]=0$ for every elementary n by n matrix $e_{k\ell}$. For any $k\not = \ell$, $[b,e_{k\ell}]=0$ implies $b_{kk}=b_{\ell\ell}$ and $b_{k\ell}=0$, showing that $b$ can be written as $b_0\otimes {\rm{Id}}\in B\otimes \mathcal{M}_n(k)$. This subalgebra is easily seen to be isomorphic to B. 
 
To show that $\mathcal{M}_n(\mbox{--}) \circ (\mbox{--})^{\mathcal{M}_n(k)} \,=\,{\rm{Id}}$, we need to check that the natural map
 
$$ \varphi\,:\,\mathcal{M}_n(k) \otimes A^{\mathcal{M}_n(k)} \rightarrow A\,,\,\,\,\, m \otimes a \mapsto \iota(m).a $$
 
is an isomorphism of involutive DG-algebras. That it is an isomorphism of DG-algebras is shown in the proof
of~\cite[Lemma 2.1]{BKR}. Further,
$$\sigma(\iota(m).a)\,=\, \sigma(a)\sigma(\iota(m)) \,=\, \sigma(a)\iota(\sigma(m)) \,=\, \iota(\sigma(m))\sigma(a) \,,$$
the last equality because $a \in A^{\mathcal{M}_n(k)}$. Hence, $\varphi$ is an isomorphism of involutive DG-algebras as desired.

title: Proposition
body_md:
\la{prep}\la{S2P1}
$\mathrm{(a)}$ The functors $$ \sqrt[n]{S \backslash \mbox{--}}\,:\,\mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_S \rightleftarrows \mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_k \,:\, \mathcal{M}_n(\mbox{--})$$
form an adjoint pair.

$\mathrm{(b)}$ The functors
  $$ (S \backslash -)^{\ob}_{n}\,:\, \mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_S \rightleftarrows \mathtt{DGCA}_k \,:\, \mathcal{M}_n(\mbox{--}) $$
  form an adjoint pair.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The functor $\mathcal{M}_n(\mbox{--}): \mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_k \rightarrow \mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_S$ is the composition of the functors
$$\begin{diagram} \mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_k & \rTo^{\mathcal{M}_n(\mbox{--})} & \mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_{\mathcal{M}_n(k)} & \rTo^{\rho^*} & \mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_S \end{diagram}\,\text{.}$$
By lemma~\ref{freeprod}, the left adjoint of the second functor in the above composition is the functor $(\mbox{--}) \ast_S \mathcal{M}_n(k)\,:\,\mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_S \rightarrow \mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_{\mathcal{M}_n(k)}$. By Lemma~\ref{eqcat}, the inverse (and hence, left adjoint) of the first functor in the above composition is the functor $(\mbox{--})^{\mathcal{M}_n(k)}$. Hence, the left adjoint of $\mathcal{M}_n(\mbox{--})\,:\,\mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_k \rightarrow \mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_S$ is the composition of functors
$$\begin{diagram} \mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_S & \rTo^{(\mbox{--}) \ast_S \mathcal{M}_n(k)} & \mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_{\mathcal{M}_n(k)} & \rTo^{(\mbox{--})^{\mathcal{M}_n(k)}} & \mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_k \end{diagram}\,,$$
which is exactly the functor $\sqrt[n]{S \backslash \mbox{--}}$. This proves (a).


It remains to show (b). The functor $\mathcal{M}_n(\mbox{--})\,:\,\mathtt{DGCA}_k \rightarrow \mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_S$ is the composition of functors
$$ \begin{diagram} \mathtt{DGCA}_k & \rTo^{(1)} & \mathtt{DGCA}^{\ob} & \rTo^{(2)} & \mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_k & \rTo^{\mathcal{M}_n(\mbox{--})} & \mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_S \end{diagram}\,,$$
where the functor labelled $(1)$ takes $B \in \mathtt{DGCA}_k$ to $B$ equipped with the trivial involution and where the functor labelled $(2)$ is the forgetful functor. The left adjoint of $(2)$ is the functor $(\mbox{--})_{\mathrm{ab}}$. The left adjoint of $(1)$ is $(\mbox{--})_{\sigma}$. Hence, (a) implies that the left adjoint of the functor $\mathcal{M}_n(\mbox{--})\,:\mathtt{DGCA}_k \rightarrow \mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_S$ is the functor
$$ (S \backslash -)^{\ob}_{n}\,:=\, (\mbox{--})_{\sigma} \circ (\mbox{--})_{\mathrm{ab}} \circ \sqrt[n]{S \backslash \mbox{--}} \,\text{.}$$ This proves (b).

title: Proof
body_md:
To simplify the notation set $ {\mathscr C} := \mathtt{DGCA}_k $ and denote by $ {\mathscr C}^{\mathscr D} $ the category of diagrams of shape $ \{\ast \leftarrow \ast \rightarrow \ast \}\,$ in $ {\mathscr C} $. The pushout construction defines a functor $\, \colim:\,{\mathscr C}^{\mathscr D} \to {\mathscr C} \,$ which is left adjoint to the diagonal functor
$ \Delta:\,{\mathscr C} \to {\mathscr C}^{\mathscr D} $ ({\it cf.} Example A.2 in \cite{BKR}). We need to show that
 
\begin{equation}
\la{coliso}
(A\bs B)^{\ob}_n   \cong \colim[\,k \xleftarrow{\,\varrho^{\ob}_n  \,} (S\bs A)^{\ob}_n    \xrightarrow{\,f^{\ob}_n  \,} (S\bs B)^{\ob}_n   \,]\ .
\end{equation}
 
To this end, we denote the above colimit by $ \colim(\varrho^{\ob}_n  ,\,f^{\ob}_n  ) $,
choose an arbitrary $ C \in \mathtt{DGCA}_k $ and identify
 
\begin{eqnarray*}
\Hom_{{\mathscr C}}(\colim(\varrho^{\ob}_n  ,\,f^{\ob}_n  ),\,C) \,\, & \cong & \Hom_{{\mathscr C}^{{\mathscr D}}}((\varrho^{\ob}_n  ,\,f^{\ob}_n  ),\,\Delta C)\\
                          &\cong  & \{\alpha \in \Hom_{{\mathscr C}}((S \bs B)^{\ob}_n  ,\,C)\ :\ \alpha\,f^{\ob}_n   = \varrho^{\ob}_n  \}\\
                          &\cong& \{\tilde{\alpha} \in \Hom_{\mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_S}(B,\,\mathcal{M}_n(k) \otimes C)\ :\ \tilde{\alpha}\,f = \varrho\}\\
                          &\cong& \Hom_{\mathtt{DGA}_A^{\ob}}(B,\,\mathcal{M}_n(k) \otimes C) \\
                          &\cong& \Hom_{\mathtt{DGCA}_k}((A \bs B)^{\ob}_n  ,\,C)\ ,
\end{eqnarray*}
 
where the third and the last bijections are given by Proposition~\ref{prep}$(b)$.
The isomorphism \eqref{coliso} follows now by Yoneda's Lemma.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Lemma~\ref{S2L9}, there is an isomorphism of functors $\, \mathtt{DGA}_A^{\ob} \to \mathtt{DGCA}_k \,$:
 
\begin{equation}\la{lccol0}
(A\bs\, \mbox{--}\,)^{\ob}_n    \cong \colim[\,k \xleftarrow{} (S\bs A)^{\ob}_n   \xrightarrow{\,(S\bs\, \mbox{--}\,)^{\ob}_n  \,} (S\bs \, \mbox{--}\,)^{\ob}_n   \,]\ .
\end{equation}
 
By uniqueness of the derived functors, \eqref{lccol0} induces an isomorphism of
functors $\, {\mathtt{Ho}}(\mathtt{DGA}_A^{\ob}) \to {\mathtt{Ho}}(\mathtt{DGCA}_k)
\,$:
 
\begin{equation}\la{lccol}
\mathbb{L}(A\bs \, \mbox{--}\,)^{\ob}_n    \cong \mathbb{L}\colim[\,k \xleftarrow{\,\varrho^{\ob}_n  \,} (S\bs A)^{\ob}_n  \xrightarrow{\,(S\bs\, \mbox{--}\,)^{\ob}_n  \,} (S\bs \, \mbox{--}\,)^{\ob}_n   \,] \ .
\end{equation}
 
Now, to compute $\,\mathbb{L} \colim \,$ in \eqref{lccol} we should replace $ f:\, A \to B $ by
its cofibrant resolution $ i:\, A \to Q(A\bs B) $ in $ \mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_A $; then
 
\begin{equation}
\la{lccol1}
\mathbb{L}\colim[\,k \xleftarrow{\,\varrho^{\ob}_n  \,} (S\bs A)^{\ob}_n    \xrightarrow{\,f^{\ob}_n  \,} (S\bs B)^{\ob}_n   \,]
\cong \gamma\,\colim[\,k \xleftarrow{\,\varrho^{\ob}_n  \,} (S \bs A)^{\ob}_n    \xrightarrow{\,i^{\ob}_n  \,} (S\bs Q(A \bs B))^{\ob}_n  \,]\ ,
\end{equation}
 
where the last `$ \colim $' is taken in $ \mathtt{DGCA}_k $ and $\,\gamma: \mathtt{DGCA}_k \to {\mathtt{Ho}}(\mathtt{DGCA}_k) \,$.

We will use a specific resolution $ i:\, A \to Q(A\bs B) $ in \eqref{lccol1}, which we construct in the following way.
First, we choose a cofibrant resolution $\,p_{S\bs A}:\, Q(S\bs A) \,\stackrel{\sim}{\twoheadrightarrow}\, A $ of $ A $ in $\,\mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_S\,$.
Then, by ~\cite[Prop. 3.1]{FHT}, there is a cofibration
$\,\tilde{f}:\, Q(S\bs A) \,\hookrightarrow\,  Q(S \bs B) \,$ in $ \mathtt{DGA}_k^{\ob} $ and a surjective quasi-isomorphism
$\,p_{S\bs B}:\, Q(S\bs B) \,\stackrel{\sim}{\twoheadrightarrow}\, B $ such that $\, p_{S\bs B} \circ \tilde{f} =
f \circ p_{S\bs A} \,$. We take $ p_{S\bs B} $ to be a cofibrant resolution of $ B $ in $ \mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_S$.
Now, we define $\, i: A \to  Q(A\bs B) $ by pushing out $ \tilde{f} $ along $ p_{S\bs A} $ in $ \mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_S \,$:
 
\begin{equation}
\la{drepd3}
\begin{diagram}[small, tight]
Q(S \bs A)                  &  \rInto^{\ \tilde{f}\ }           & Q(S \bs B) \\
\dOnto^{\,p_{S \bs A}\,}   &                                   & \dOnto^{\tilde{\varphi}} \\
A                           &  \rInto^{i\ }                     & Q(A\bs B)
\end{diagram}
\end{equation}
 
By the universal property of pushouts, there is a (unique) morphism $\,p_{A \bs B}:\,Q(A\bs B) \to B \,$ 
in $ \mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_S $ such that $\,p_{A \bs B} \circ i = f \,$ and  $\,p_{A\bs B} \circ \tilde{\varphi} = p_{S\bs B}\,$. We claim that $ p_{A \bs B} $ is a cofibrant resolution 
of $ f $ in $ \mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_A $. Indeed, by \cite[Prop. 3.14]{DS}, $\,i\,$ is a cofibration in $ \mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_k $, 
so $ Q(S \bs A) $ is a cofibrant object in $ \mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_S $. On the other hand,  $\, \tilde{\varphi} \,$  is a pushout of a quasi-isomorphism along a cofibration in $ \mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_k $, hence, by Proposition~\ref{dgproper}, this map is a quasi-isomorphism as 
well. Finally, $\,p_{A\bs B} \circ \tilde{\varphi} = p_{S\bs B}\,$ implies that
$ p_{A\bs B} $ is a surjective quasi-isomorphism, since so is $ p_{S \bs B} $.

Now, since $\,(S\bs \, \mbox{--}\,)^{\ob}_n  : \mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_S \to \mathtt{DGCA}_k\,$ is a left adjoint functor,
it preserves colimits: hence, it follows from \eqref{drepd3} that
 
\begin{equation}
\la{drepd33}
(S \bs Q(A\bs B))^{\ob}_n    \cong \colim[\,(S\bs A)^{\ob}_n   \xleftarrow{} Q(S\bs A)^{\ob}_n   \xrightarrow{\tilde{f}^{\ob}_n  } Q(S\bs B)^{\ob}_n   \,]
\end{equation}
 
On the other hand, since $\,(S\bs \, \mbox{--}\,)^{\ob}_n   \,$ is a left Quillen functor, it preserves cofibrations:
hence $ \tilde{f}^{\ob}_n   $ in \eqref{drepd33} is a cofibration in $ \mathtt{DGCA}_k $ since so is $ \tilde{f} $ in \eqref{drepd3}.
Combining \eqref{lccol}, \eqref{lccol1} and \eqref{drepd33}, we get
 
\begin{eqnarray*}
\mathbb{L}(A\bs B\,)^{\ob}_n  
&\cong&
\gamma\,\colim[\,k \xleftarrow{ \tilde{\varrho}^{\ob}_n   } Q(S\bs A)^{\ob}_n    \xrightarrow{\tilde{f}^{\ob}_n  } Q(S\bs B)^{\ob}_n   \,] \nonumber \\*[1ex]
&\cong&
\colim[\,k \xleftarrow{ \gamma \tilde{\varrho}^{\ob}_n   } \gamma\,Q(S\bs A)^{\ob}_n  
\xrightarrow{\gamma \tilde{f}^{\ob}_n  } \gamma\, Q(S\bs B)^{\ob}_n   \,] \la{drepd34} \\*[1ex]
&\cong &
\colim[\,k \xleftarrow{\,\mathbb{L}(\varrho)^{\ob}_n  \,} \mathbb{L}(S\bs A)^{\ob}_n    \xrightarrow{\,\mathbb{L}(f)^{\ob}_n  \,} \mathbb{L}(S\bs B)^{\ob}_n   \,] \la{drepd35} \ ,
\end{eqnarray*}
 
where the second isomorphism is a consequence of ~\cite[Prop. A.2]{BKR}, and the third holds by Theorem~\ref{trep}.
Note that ~\cite[Prop. A.2]{BKR} applies in our situation, since $ \mathtt{DGCA}_k $ is a proper model category
({\it cf.} Proposition~\ref{dgproper}).

title: Theorem
body_md:
\la{EMsps}
Given $\, S \xrightarrow{} A \xrightarrow{} B\,$ in ${\mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_k}^+$ and a representation $ A \to \mathcal{M}_n(k) $,
there is an Eilenberg-Moore spectral sequence with
 
$$
E^2_{\ast,\,\ast} = {\rm{Tor}}_{\ast,\,\ast}^{\mathrm{HR}^{\ob}_\bullet(S\bs A, k^n)}(k,\,\mathrm{HR}^{\ob}_\bullet(S \bs B, k^n))
$$
 
converging to $ \mathrm{HR}^{\ob}_{\bullet}(A\bs B, k^n) $.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
To construct this spectral sequence we will use the cofibrant resolutions
constructed in the proof of Theorem~\ref{hopushout}.
In addition, we will assume that $ Q(R\bs S) $ is chosen to be almost free
in $ \mathtt{DGA}_R^{\ob,+} $ ({\it cf.}  \cite[Prop. 3.1]{FHT}).
Then the pushout diagram \eqref{drepd3} gives the pushout
in the category $ \mathtt{DGCA}_k^+ $:
 
\begin{equation}
\la{dred}
\begin{diagram}[small, tight]
Q(R\bs S)^{\ob}_n     &  \rTo^{\tilde{f}^{\ob}_n  } & Q(R \bs A)^{\ob}_n   \\
\dTo^{\tilde{\varrho}^{\ob}_n  } &          & \dTo \\
k             &  \rInto             & Q(S \bs A)^{\ob}_n  
\end{diagram}
\end{equation}
 
where $\, \tilde{\varrho}^{\ob}_n   :\,Q(R\bs S)^{\ob}_n   \to  k \,$ is the map adjoint to
$\,\tilde{\varrho} := \varrho \circ p_{R\bs S}: Q(R\bs S) \to \mathcal{M}_n(k) \,$.
It follows from \eqref{dred} that
 
$$
k \otimes_{Q(R \bs S )^{\ob}_n  } Q(R \bs A)^{\ob}_n   \cong Q(S\bs A)^{\ob}_n   \ .
$$
 
Moreover, for the almost free DG resolutions $\, Q(R\bs S),\,Q(R \bs A)\,$ and $\, Q(S \bs A)\,$,
the commutative DG algebras $ Q(R\bs S)^{\ob}_n  ,\,Q(R \bs A)^{\ob}_n   $ and $ Q(S \bs A)^{\ob}_n   $
are almost free. The existence of the Eilenberg-Moore spectral is now standard (see, e.g.,
\cite{McC}, Theorem~7.6).

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix a cofibrant resolution $Q(S\bs A) \to S\bs A \in \mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_S$. Then, for any $C\in \mathtt{CAlg}_k^*$, there are natural isomorphisms

\begin{eqnarray*}
\Hom_{\mathtt{CAlg}_k^*}((S\bs A)_n,\,C) \,\,& \cong & \Hom_{\mathtt{Alg}^{\ob}_S}(A,\,\mathcal{M}_n(k) \otimes C)\\
                          &\cong  & \Hom_{\mathtt{DGA}^{\ast,+}_S}(Q(S \bs A),\, \mathcal{M}_n(k) \otimes C)\\
                          &\cong& \Hom_{\mathtt{DGCA}^{\ast,+}_k}(Q(S \bs A)_n ,\, C)\\
                          &\cong& \Hom_{\mathtt{CAlg}_k^*}(\mathrm H_0[Q(S \bs A)_n],\, C)\ ,
\end{eqnarray*}
The first isomorphism is a degree 0 (underived) application of \ref{prep}(a).
 
The second isomorphism was due to the fact that $\mathcal{M}_n(k) \otimes C$ is concentrated in degree 0.
 
The third isomorphism is \ref{prep}(b)
 
The fourth ismorphism is again a statement about $C$ being concentrated in degree 0.

title: Theorem
body_md:
\la{inv}\la{S2P4}
$(a)$ The functor $(-)_n^{\ast,G}$ has a total left derived functor
$$
\mathbb{L}[(\,-\,)_n^{\ast, G}]:\,{\mathtt{Ho}}(\mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_k) \to {\mathtt{Ho}}(\mathtt{DGCA}_k)\ .
$$
 

$(b)$ There is an isomorphism of functors
 
$\,
\mathbb{L}[(\,-\,)_n^{\ast,G}] \cong [\mathbb{L}(\,-\,)^{\ob}_n]^{G}
\,$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
$(a)$ By ~\cite{BKR} Lemma A.2, it suffices to show that $\,(-)_n^{\ast,G}$ maps any acyclic cofibration $\,i: A \,\stackrel{\sim}{\,\hookrightarrow\,}\, B \,$ between cofibrant objects in $\mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_k$ to a weak equivalence in $\mathtt{DGCA}_k$. By ~\cite{BKR} A4.8, given $\,i: A \,\stackrel{\sim}{\,\hookrightarrow\,}\, B \,$, there is a map $\,p:B \rightarrow A\,$ in $\mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_k$ such that $\,pi={\rm{Id}}_A\,$ and $ip$ is homotopic to ${\rm{Id}}_B$. Hence, $p^{G} \circ i^G= {\rm{Id}}_{(A)_n^{\ast,G}}$. By Proposition \ref{lhom}, there is a morphism $\,h:B \rightarrow B \otimes \Omega $ in $\mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_k$ with $\,h(0)={\rm{Id}}_B\,$ and $\,h(1)=ip\,$. By the obvious analog (in the involutive setting) of \cite[Lemma 2.5]{BKR}, there is a morphism $h^G:(B)_n^{\ast,G} \rightarrow (B)_n^{\ast,G} \otimes \Omega $ such that $h^G(0)={\rm{Id}}_{(B)_n^{\ast,G}}$ and $h^G(1)=i^G \circ p^G$. Finally, by Proposition~\ref{lhom}, $i^G \circ p^G$ induces the identity map at the level of homology. Hence $i^G$ is a weak equivalence in $\mathtt{DGCA}_k$. This proves $(a)$.

$(b)$ The functor $ \mathbb{L}[(-)_n^{\ast,G}] $ maps $\,\gamma A \in {\mathtt{Ho}}(\mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_k)\,$ to the class of the invariant subalgebra $ (QA)_n^{\ast,G} $ of $ (QA)_n^{\ob}$, where $ QA $ is a cofibrant replacement of $A$. By $(a)$, this map is well-defined, i.e. does not depend on the choice of $ QA $. On the other hand, $ \mathrm{HR}_{\bullet}^{\ob}(\mbox{--})_n^{\ast,G} $ maps $ \gamma A $ to $\mathrm{HR}_{\bullet}^{\ob}( [\gamma(QA)^{\ob}_n])^G $. Since $k$ is of characteristic $0$ and since $\GL(V)$ is reductive, $\,\mathrm{HR}_{\bullet}^*(\gamma[((QA)_n^{\ob})^G]) \cong [\mathrm{HR}_{\bullet}^*(\gamma((QA)_n^{\ob}))]^G \,$ for all $A \in \mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_k$. This proves part $(b)$.

title: Proposition
body_md:
\la{ptan1}
 The tangent complex to the DG-scheme $\mathrm{Spec }A_n^*$ at the closed point $\rho$ is precisely
the subcomplex $\mathrm{Der}^{\rho}_{\bullet}(A,\mathcal{M}_n(k))^{\mathbb{Z}_2}$ of elements of $\mathrm{Der}^{\rho}_{\bullet}(A,\mathcal{M}_n(k))$
that are fixed by the above $\mathbb{Z}_2$-action.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Indeed, the required tangent complex is the complex $\mathrm{Der}^{\rho}_{\bullet}(A_n^*,k)$. Note that for a fixed (homological)
degree $i$, $\mathrm{Der}_{-i}^{\rho}(A_n^*,k)\,=\,\Hom_{\mathtt{DGCA}_k}^{\rho}(A_n^*,k[\epsilon]/\epsilon^2)$ where $\epsilon$ is
homogenous of degree $i$ and where the superscript $\rho$ indicates that we consider only those homomorphisms which equal $\rho\,:A_n^* \rightarrow k$
after composition with the augmentation $k[\epsilon]/\epsilon^2 \rightarrow k$.

By Proposition~\ref{prep}, we have the identification
$$ \Hom_{\mathtt{DGCA}_k}^{\rho}(A_n^*,k[\epsilon]/\epsilon^2)\,=\,\Hom_{\mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_k}^{\rho}(A,\mathcal{M}_n(k) \otimes k[\epsilon]/\epsilon^2)\,\text{.}$$
On the other hand,
$\Hom_{\mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_k}^{\rho}(A,\mathcal{M}_n(k) \otimes k[\epsilon]/\epsilon^2)$ is precisely the set of $\rho$-derivations $D$ of degree $-i$
satisfying

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $\mathtt{Alg}^{\ob}_k$ is the category of algebras over an operad, the monoidal Dold-Kan correspondence (see \cite[Theorem A.1]{BRYII}) implies that there is a Quillen equivalence 

$$ N^{\ast}\,:\,{\mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_k}^+ \rightleftarrows \mathtt{s}\mathtt{Alg}^{\ob}_k\,:\,N\,,\qquad N^{\ast}\,:\,\mathtt{DGCA}_k^+ \rightleftarrows \mathtt{s}\mathtt{CAlg}_k\,:\,N$$

where ${\mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_k}^+$ (resp., $\mathtt{DGCA}_k^+$) stands for the category of involutive DG algebras (resp., commutative DG algebras) concentrated in nonnegative homological degree and $N$ stands for the normalized chain complex functor. These Quillen equivalences fit into a commutative diagram of functors 
 
\[
\begin{diagram}[small]
 {\mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_k}^+ & \rTo^{N^{\ast}} & \mathtt{s}\mathtt{Alg}^{\ob}_k\\
  \dTo^{(\mbox{--})^{\ob}_n} & & \dTo_{(\mbox{--})^{\ob}_n}\\
 \mathtt{DGCA}_k^+ & \rTo^{N^{\ast}} & \mathtt{s}\mathtt{CAlg}_k\\
\end{diagram}\ .
\]
   
View $A\in \mathtt{Alg}^{\ob}_k$ as a (discrete) object in $\mathtt{s}\mathtt{Alg}^{\ob}_k$. Then $N^{\ast}(QA)$ is a cofibrant resolution of $A$ in $\mathtt{s}\mathtt{Alg}^{\ob}_k$ for any cofibrant resolution $QA$ of $A$ in ${\mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_k}^+$. Hence, 
 
\begin{align*}
\mathrm{HR}_\bullet^{\ob}(A,k^n)^{\mathtt{s}} & \cong  \pi_\bullet[(N^{\ast}(QA))^{\ob}_n]\\
                                    & \cong \pi_\bullet[N^{\ast}((QA)^{\ob}_n))]\\
                                    &\cong \mathrm H_\bullet[NN^{\ast}((QA)^{\ob}_n))]\\
                                    & \cong \mathrm H_\bullet[(QA)^{\ob}_n]\\
                                    & \cong \mathrm{HR}_\bullet^{\ob}(A,k^n)
\end{align*}
 
This proves the desired proposition.

We recall that $\, \Omega = k[t] \oplus k[t] dt \,$ denotes the algebraic de Rham complex of $ \mathbb{A}^1_k $, which is a commutative
DG algebra. The natural maps $\,B \,\hookrightarrow\, B \otimes \Omega \hookleftarrow \Omega \,$ induce then an isomorphism of complexes $\,B_\n \otimes \Omega \xrightarrow{\sim} (B \otimes \Omega)_\n \,$.
Identifying these complexes, we have the commutative diagram
 
\begin{equation*}
\begin{diagram}[small, tight]
S_{\natural} & \rTo  & B_{\natural} \otimes \Omega\\
             & \rdTo & \dTo_{{\rm{Id}} \otimes {\rm{ev}}_a}\\
             &       & B_{\natural}
\end{diagram}
\end{equation*}
 
which induces a map of c\^{o}nes $\,\widetilde{{\rm{ev}}}_a:\,
\cn(S_\n \to B_\n \otimes \Omega)\,\to \,\cn(S_\n \to B_\n)\,$
for each $ a \in k $. (Here, $ {\rm{ev}}_a:\, \Omega \to k $ stands for
the evaluation map $\,f(t) + g(t) dt \mapsto f(a)\,$, where $ a \in k $.)

If we now apply $ \mathcal{C} $ to $ h $, we get a morphism
 
$$
\mathcal{C}(h):\,\cn(S_\n \to A_\n)\,\to \,\cn(S_\n \to B_\n \otimes \Omega)\ ,
$$
 
such that $\,\mathcal{C}(h)(0) := \widetilde{{\rm{ev}}}_0 \circ \mathcal{C}(h) = \mathcal{C}(f) \,$ and $\,\mathcal{C}(h)(1) := \widetilde{{\rm{ev}}}_1 \circ \mathcal{C}(h) =
\mathcal{C}(g) \,$. To show that $\,\mathcal{C}(f) \sim \mathcal{C}(g) \,$ it thus suffices to show that

the fact that, for all $ a \in k \,$, $\,{\rm{ev}}_a \sim {\rm{ev}}_0\,$ as morphisms $ \Omega \to k $;
the corresponding homotopy $ \Omega \to k[1] $ is given by $\,f(t)+ g(t)\,dt \mapsto \int_0^a\,g(\tau)\,d\tau\,$.

title: Theorem

\la{dihedral}
 The functor $\mathcal{C}\,:\,\mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_S \rightarrow \mathtt{Com}_k$ has a total left derived functor
$$ \mathbb{L} \mathcal{C}\,:\, {\mathtt{Ho}}(\mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_S) \rightarrow \mathcal D(k)\,,\,\,\,\, \gamma S \bs A \mapsto \gamma \mathcal{C}(S \bs QA) $$
where $S \bs QA $ is a cofibrant resolution of $S \bs A$ in $\mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_S$.

title: Proof
body_md:
The proof is analogous to the proof of Theorem~\ref{inv}. By Brown's Lemma (~\cite[Proposition A.2]{BKR}), it suffices to show that $\,\mathcal{C}\,$ maps
acyclic cofibrations $\,i: A \,\stackrel{\sim}{\,\hookrightarrow\,}\, B \,$ between cofibrant objects in $\mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_S $ to weak equivalences
(quasi-isomorphisms) in $\mathtt{Com}(k) $. Given $\,i: A \,\stackrel{\sim}{\,\hookrightarrow\,}\, B \,$, there is a map $\,p:\,B \to A\,$ in $\mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_S$ such that
$\,p\,i={\rm{Id}}_A\,$ and $\,i\,p \sim {\rm{Id}}_B\,$ ({\it cf.} \cite[Proposition A.1]{BKR}). Hence $ \mathcal{C}(p) \,\circ\, \mathcal{C}(i) = {\rm{Id}}_{\mathcal{C}(A)} $, and
by Proposition~\ref{lhom}, there is a morphism $\,h: B \rightarrow B \otimes \Omega $ in $\mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_S $
with $\,h(0)={\rm{Id}}_B\,$ and $\,h(1)=i\,p\,$. Lemma~\ref{goodhom} now implies that $ \mathcal{C}(ip) \sim {\rm{Id}}_{\mathcal{C}(B)} $.
Hence $ \mathcal{C}(i p) $ induces the identity map on homology, and therefore $ \mathcal{C}(i) $ is a quasi-isomorphism.

We verify the assumptions of Brown's Lemma for $ \widetilde{\mathcal{C}} $. Let $ A \to B $ be a
cofibrant object in $ \mathtt{Mor}(\mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_k)$, which means that $ A \to B $ is a cofibration
in $ \mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_k $, with $A$ being a cofibrant object.
Let
 
\begin{equation*}
\begin{diagram}[small, tight]
A                 & \rTo^{\alpha}    &  C         \\
\dTo          &                      & \dTo   \\
B                 & \rTo^{\beta}     &  D
\end{diagram}
\end{equation*}
 
be an acyclic cofibration in $ \mathtt{Mor}(\mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_k) $, which means that
$ \alpha $ is an acyclic cofibration, $\, \beta $ is a weak equivalence, and
the induced map $\, B \coprod_A C \to D \,$ is a cofibration in $ \mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_k $.
Since $ A \,\hookrightarrow\, B $ is a cofibration, the pushout $ B \to B \coprod_A C $ of $ \alpha $
along $ A \to B $ is an acyclic cofibration. Since
$\,\beta:\, B \to B \coprod_A C \to D $ is acyclic, the cofibration
$\, B \coprod_A C \to D \,$ is also acyclic. It follows that
$ \beta $ itself is an acyclic cofibration. The standard argument
(see the proof of Theorem~\ref{mordih} above) implies now that $ \alpha_\n $ and
$ \beta_\n $ are quasi-isomorphisms. Hence, the pair
$(\alpha_\n,\,\beta_\n) $ induces a quasi-isomorphism
$\,\widetilde{\mathcal{C}}(A \bs B) \xrightarrow{\sim} \widetilde{\mathcal{C}}(C \bs D) \,$.
By Brown's Lemma, $\, \mathbb{L}\widetilde{\mathcal{C}} $ exists and is given by formula
\eqref{isff}, which is independent of the choice of resolutions.

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix a cofibrant resolution $\, p_R: QR \,\stackrel{\sim}{\twoheadrightarrow}\, R \,$ in $ \mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_k $. Then choose cofibrant resolutions $\, p_S: QS \,\stackrel{\sim}{\twoheadrightarrow}\, S \,$ of $ g \circ p_R $ in $ \mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_{QR} $ and
$p_A: QA \,\stackrel{\sim}{\twoheadrightarrow}\, A\,$ of $ f\circ p_S $ in $ \mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_{QS}$. Note that both $QS$ and $QA$ are cofibrant
in $ \mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_k $, and there are liftings $ \tilde{g}: QR \,\hookrightarrow\, QS $ and  $ \tilde{f}: QS \,\hookrightarrow\, QA $ which are cofibrations.
Now, by Octahedron Axiom, associated to $ (QR)_\n \xrightarrow{\tilde{g}} (QS)_\n \xrightarrow{\tilde{f}} (QA)_\n $
is a distinguished triangle in $ {\mathscr D}(k)$ of the form
 
$$
\la{isct}
\cn(\tilde{g}_\n) \to \cn(\tilde{f}_\n \circ \tilde{g}_\n) \to \cn(\tilde{f}_\n) \to \cn(\tilde{g}_\n)[1] \ .
$$
 
By \eqref{isff}, $\,\mathbb{L}\widetilde{\mathcal{C}}(g) = \cn(\tilde{g}_\n)$, and similarly for $f$ and $ f \, g $. The above triangle is thus isomorphic to \eqref{isct}.

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\sigma$ denote the skew involution on $C$. One can define an involution on the graded algebra $T(\overline{C}[-1])$ whose restriction to the (graded) generating space $\overline{C}[-1]$ is $\sigma$. Denote this extended involution on $T(\overline{C}[-1])$ by $\sigma$ as well. It remains to check that $\sigma \circ d=d \circ \sigma$, where $d$ is the differential on $\mathbf{\Omega}(C)$.
Since $\sigma \circ d$ and $d \circ \sigma$ are both derivations from $\mathbf{\Omega}(C)$ to $\mathbf{\Omega}(C)^{\rm op}$ with respect to the graded algebra homomorphism $\sigma$, it suffices to check that they coincide on generators, i.e, when restricted to $\overline{C}[-1]$. Recall that $d=d_1+d_2$. That $\sigma$ (restricted to $\overline{C}[-1]$ commutes with $d_1$ follows from the fact that $\sigma:C \rightarrow C$ is a map of complexes. That $\sigma$ (restricted to $\overline{C}[-1]$ commutes with $d_2$ follows from the fact that it is a skew-involution on $C$: indeed, for $x \in \overline{C}$ we have (using Sweedler notation for coproducts)

\begin{align*}
\sigma(d_2(s^{-1}x)) &=\sigma \big({\rm Sw}(-s^{-1} \otimes s^{-1} \otimes x^{(1)} \otimes x^{(2)})\big) \text{ (by \eqref{d2})} \\
 &= -(-1)^{|x^{(1)}|}\sigma(s^{-1}x^{(1)}\otimes s^{-1}x^{(2)}) \\   
 &= (-1)^{(|x^{(1)}|-1)|x^{(2)}|}(\sigma(s^{-1}x^{(2)})\otimes \sigma(s^{-1}x^{(1)}))\\
 &= (-1)^{|x^{(1)}||x^{(2)}|}{\rm Sw}\big(s^{-1} \otimes s^{-1} \otimes \sigma(x^{(2)}) \otimes \sigma(x^{(1)})\big)\\
&= {\rm Sw}\big(-s^{-1} \otimes s^{-1} \otimes -\tau \circ (\sigma \otimes \sigma)(x^{(1)} \otimes x^{(2)})\big)\\
&= {\rm Sw}\big(-s^{-1} \otimes s^{-1} \otimes \Delta(\sigma(x))\big) \text{ (since $C$ is skew involutive)}\\
&=  d_2(s^{-1}\sigma(x))=d_2(\sigma(s^{-1}x)) \ .\\
\end{align*}

   &= - \sigma_R \circ  m_R \circ \left[ (f \otimes g) \circ \tau \circ (\sigma_C \otimes \sigma_C) \circ \Delta_C  \right]\\

title: Proof

Recall \cite[Def. 5.2, Thm. 5.4]{G22} that Graves constructed a functor that we will call $G(\mbox{--}):\mathtt{Alg}^{\ob}_k \to \mathrm{sE}_\infty\mathtt{Alg}_k$, taking $A\to C(\Delta H_+,\mathrm H_{A+})$, such that  $\pi_\bullet[GA] \cong {\rm HO}_\bullet(A)$ for any

Here, $\mathrm{sE}_\infty\mathtt{Alg}_k$ denotes the category of $E_{\infty}$-algebra objects in the category of simplicial $k$-modules (which we shall refer to as {\it simplicial $E_{\infty}$-algebras}). Here, the term `$E_{\infty}$-algebra' refers to an algebra over the simplicial $E_{\infty}$-operad $\mathcal{D}_{\bf Mod}$, an analogue of the Barratt-Eccles operad in \cite{G21} (with notation mirroring \cite[Remark 2.8]{Au2}). Now let $A \in \mathtt{s}\mathtt{Alg}^{\ob}_k$ be an arbitrary simplicial involutive $k$-algebra. Then, $GA$ is a bisimplicial $E_\infty$-algebra whose diagonal $k$-module is an $E_{\infty}$-algebra. Let $\Delta H_+$ be the category obtained by adjoining an initial object $[-1]$ to $\Delta H$. Now recall that, by definition (see \cite[Defn. 2.5, Defn. 6.3]{G21} and \cite[Theorem 5.4]{G22}),
 
$$GA = k[N(\mbox{--}\downarrow \Delta H_+)] \otimes_{\Delta H_+} B_{\rm hOct,+}A \,,
$$
 
where $N(\mbox{--})$ stands for the simplicial nerve functor and $B_{\rm hOct,+}A$ is the extension of $B_{\rm hOct}(A)$ to a $\Delta H_+$-module as in \cite[Def. 6.3]{G21}. Since the simplicial right $\Delta H_+$-module $k[N(\mbox{--}\downarrow \Delta H_+)]$ is a levelwise projective resolution of $k$, the homology of (the Dold-Kan normalization of) the diagonal of $GA$ is precisely
 
$${\rm Tor}^{\Delta H_+}_\bullet(k, B_{\rm hOct,+}A)\, \cong\, {\rm Tor}^{\Delta H}_\bullet(k, B_{\rm hOct}(A)) = : \mathrm{HO}_\bullet(A)\ . $$
 
The above isomorphism is \cite[Thm 6.4]{G21}. This proves the desired lemma.

title: Proof
body_md:
Given an algebra $A$, we can construct the map \eqref{SRAA} as follows. Fix a semi-free simplicial resolution $R \stackrel{\sim}{\to} A$ in $\mathtt{s}\mathtt{Alg}^{\ob}_k $ and consider the natural map
 
\begin{equation}\la{dttot} k \otimes^{\mathbb{L}}_{\Delta H} {\rm C}(B_{\rm hOct}(R)) \to  k \otimes_{\Delta H} {\rm C}(B_{\rm hOct}(R))  \end{equation}
 
where ${\rm C}$ stands for the associated chain complex. By the K\"{u}nneth Theorem, $B_{\rm hOct}(R) \xrightarrow{\sim} B_{\rm hOct}(A)$ is a weak equivalence. Hence $\mathrm H_\bullet[k \otimes^{\mathbb{L}}_{\Delta H} {\rm C}(B_{\rm hOct}(R))] \cong \mathrm{HO}_\bullet(A)$. Note that there are natural isomorphisms of simplicial $k$-vector spaces $k \otimes_{\Delta H} B_{\rm hOct}(R) \cong R_{\rm ab,\sigma} \cong (R)_1^{\ob}$, where $R_{\rm ab,\sigma}$ denotes the quotient of the abelianization $R_{\rm ab}$ of $R$ by the ideal generated by the image of ${\rm{Id}} -\sigma$ ($\sigma$ being the induced involution on $R_{\rm ab}$). The first of these isomophisms is by \cite[Thm 5.8]{G22}, while the second isomorphism is by definition (see Section \ref{SDRep}). Hence $\mathrm H_\bullet[k \otimes_{\Delta H} {\rm C}(B_{\rm hOct}(R))] \cong \mathrm{HR^{\ob}_{\bullet}}(A,k)$.Thus, \eqref{dttot} induces on homology a graded $k$-linear map $\mathrm{Tr}_{\rm sym}(A)_\bullet:\mathrm{HO}_\bullet(A) \to \mathrm{HR^{\ob}_{\bullet}}(A,k)$. 
 
 Next, note that the map ${\rm{Tr}}_1(R):R_{\natural} \to (R)^{\ob}_1$ inducing ${\rm{Tr}}(A)_\bullet$ is just the canonical quotient to $(R)^{\ob}_1:=R_{\rm ab, \sigma}$, and the map $i^{\ast}$ coincides with $ {\rm{Tr}}_1(R) : k \otimes_{\Delta D^{\rm op}} B^{\rm dih}R \to k \otimes_{\Delta H} B_{\rm hOct}(R)$ when restricted to the non-derived tensor products. Hence the following diagram commutes in 
 $ {\mathscr D}(k) $: 
  
 $$  
 \begin{diagram}[small]
   k \otimes^{\mathbb{L}}_{\Delta D^{\rm op}} {\rm C}(B^{\rm dih}R)  & \rTo^{i^{\ast}} & k \otimes^{\mathbb{L}}_{\Delta H} {\rm C}(B_{\rm hOct}(R))\\
    \dTo & & \dTo\\
   k \otimes_{\Delta D^{\rm op}} {\rm C}(B^{\rm dih}R) & \rTo^{{\rm{Tr}}_1(R)} &  k \otimes_{\Delta H} {\rm C}(B_{\rm hOct}(R))\\
 \end{diagram}
 $$
  
 which gives the natural isomorphism $ \mathrm{Tr}_{\rm hOct}(A)_\bullet \circ i^* \cong {\rm{Tr}}(A)_\bullet $ on homology.

 
 It remains to prove that the map \eqref{SRAA} constructed above is an algebra homomorphism. To this end,
consider the bisimplicial $E_{\infty}$-algebra $G{R}_\bullet$, where $G(\mbox{--})_\bullet:\mathtt{Alg}^{\ob}_k \to \mathrm{sE}_\infty\mathtt{Alg}_k$ is Grave's functor (see the proof of Lemma \ref{algstr}) .The total (i.e. diagonal) simplicial vector space of $GR_\bullet$ is a (simplicial) $E_{\infty}$-algebra.
Recall that 
$$GR_{\bullet}  = k[(N(\mbox{--}\downarrow \Delta H_+))_i] \otimes_{\Delta H_+} B_{\rm hOct,+}R \ .
$$
 
This is a (bi)simplicial vector spaceoverl, and as in (the proof of) \cite[Lemma 3.1]{Au2}, 
$$GR_{i} \,\cong\, \bigoplus_{[n]\stackrel{{\rm{Id}}}{\to} [n] \stackrel{f_1}{\to} [n_1] \stackrel{f_2}{\to} \ldots \stackrel{f_i}{\to} [n_i]} R^{\otimes n}\,,$$
where the direct sum runs over chains of morphisms $[n]\stackrel{{\rm{Id}}}{\to} [n] \stackrel{f_1}{\to} [n_1] \stackrel{f_2}{\to} \ldots \stackrel{f_i}{\to} [n_i]$ of length $i+1$ in $\Delta H_+$. Since 
$$ GA_{i} \,\cong\, \bigoplus_{[n]\stackrel{{\rm{Id}}}{\to} [n] \stackrel{f_1}{\to} [n_1] \stackrel{f_2}{\to} \ldots \stackrel{f_i}{\to} [n_i]}  A^{\otimes n} \,,$$
$GR_i \to GA_i$ is a weak equivalence for all $i$ by the K\"{u}nneth theorem. Hence, $GR_\bullet \to GA_\bullet$ is a weak equivalence of simplicial $E_{\infty}$-algebras.
Hence, ${\tt diag}(G{R}_\bullet) \xrightarrow{\sim} {\tt diag}(GA_\bullet)$ is a quasi-isomorphism of $E_{\infty}$-algebras. On the other hand, the natural map $G(R_i) \to \mathrm{HO}_0(R_i) \cong (R_i)_{\rm ab,\sigma}$ is an $E_{\infty}$-algebra homomorphism by \cite[Thm 6.8]{G22}, where $R_i$ is the algebra of $i$-simplices on $R$. 
Hence the map ${\tt diag}(GR_\bullet) \to R_{\rm ab, \sigma}$ is a map of $E_{\infty}$-algebras.
Since the map $C(R_i) \to \mathrm{HO}_0(R_i) \cong (R_i)_{\rm ab,\sigma}$ represents the map $k \otimes^{\mathbb{L}}_{\Delta H} B_{\rm hOct}(R)_i \to k \otimes_{\Delta H} B_{\rm hOct}(R)_i$, the map induced on homology (of the associated chain complexes) by the map ${\tt diag}(GR_\bullet) \to R_{\rm ab, \sigma}$ is the same as that induced on homologies by \eqref{dttot}, which is $\mathrm{Tr}_{\rm hOct}(A)_\bullet$. Since the map ${\tt diag}(GR) \to R_{\rm ab, \sigma}$ is a homomorphism of simplicial $E_{\infty}$-algebras, $\mathrm{Tr}_{\rm hOct}(A)_\bullet$ is a morphism of graded commutative algebras. This finishes the proof of the proposition.

title: Proposition
body_md:
\la{pC}
Let V be a k-vector space. Then
$${\rm{Tor}}_i^{\Delta H}(k, B_{\rm hOct}(F(V)))\simeq  \begin{cases}
{\rm{Sym}}(V)
   & \text{ if }  i=0 \\
0
   & \text{ if } i\not = 0
\end{cases}$$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Choose a basis in V, say a set $X\subset V$, so that $F(V)\cong F(k[X]) \cong k[J(X)]$, where $J(X)$ denotes the free involutive monoid generated by the set, that is, the classical James construction applied to the (based) set $(C_2 \times X)_+:= (C_2 \times X) \sqcup \{\ast\}$ (with $\ast$ regarded as the basepoint). We regard $J(X)$ as the $C_2$-James construction of the discrete (based) space $X_+$, where, as in \cite{G21}, the classical James construction as an endofunctor of $Top_*$ has been extended an endofunctor of $C_2-Top_*$ according to the rule $t(x_1,...,x_n)=(tx_n,...,tx_1)$. Then, by \cite[Lemma 7.13]{G21} and (the proof of) \cite[Lemma 15]{G21}, we have 
$$
{\rm HO}_\bullet(F(V))\, \cong\, {\rm HO}_\bullet(k[J(X)])\, \cong \, \mathrm H_\bullet[\mathcal{N}X; k]\ ,
$$ 
 
where 
 
$$\mathcal{N}X \,:=\, \coprod_{n \geq -1} N([n] \downarrow \Delta H_+) \times_{H_{n+1}} (C_2 \times X)^{n+1}\ . $$
 
                                                                                                                                                                        
 
Here, $\Delta H_+$ is the category obtained by adding to $\Delta H$ the initial object $[-1]$, and $N(\mbox{--})$ in the formula above stands for the nerve. By \cite[Lemma 7.16]{G21}, there is a weak equivalence $\mathcal{N}X \simeq \mathcal{D}X$, where 
 
$$\mathcal{D}X\,:=\, \coprod_{n \geqslant 0} E_{\ast}H_{n} \times_{H_{n}} (C_2 \times  X)^{n}\ . $$
 
Hence,
 
\begin{align*} 
{\rm HO}_\bullet(F(V)) &\cong\,\mathrm H_\bullet[\mathcal{D}X; k] \\
                       & \cong\, \operatorname*{\text{\raisebox{0.25ex}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\bigoplus$}}}}_{n=0}^{\infty} \mathrm H_\bullet\left(k[E_{\ast}H_{n}] \otimes_{k[H_n]} k[C_2 \times X]^{\otimes n}\right)\\
                       & \cong\,  \operatorname*{\text{\raisebox{0.25ex}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\bigoplus$}}}}_{n=0}^{\infty} \mathrm H_\bullet \left( k[E_{\ast}H_{n}] \otimes_{k[H_n]} k[k[C_2] \otimes V]^{\otimes n}\right)\\
                       & \cong\, \operatorname*{\text{\raisebox{0.25ex}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\bigoplus$}}}}_{n=0}^{\infty} \mathrm H_\bullet \left( k \otimes^{\mathbb{L}}_{k[H_n]} k[k[C_2] \otimes V]^{\otimes n}\right)\\
                      & \cong\,  \operatorname*{\text{\raisebox{0.25ex}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\bigoplus$}}}}_{n=0}^{\infty} \mathrm H_\bullet \left(H_n,(k[C_2] \otimes V)^{\otimes n}\right)\\
                      &\cong\, \operatorname*{\text{\raisebox{0.25ex}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\bigoplus$}}}}_{n=0}^{\infty} \mathrm H_0 \left(H_n,(k[C_2] \otimes V)^{\otimes n}\right)\\
                      & \cong\, {\rm HO}_0(F(V))\\
                      & \cong\,{\rm{Sym}}(V)\ .\\
\end{align*}
 
The third isomorphism is above is because $X$ is a discrete basis of $V$. Since $E_{\ast}H_n$ is contractible for all $n$, $k[E_\ast H_n]$ is weakly equivalent to $k$. Further, $k[E_\bullet \mathrm H_n]$ is a levelwise projective simplicial right $\Sigma_n$-module. This explains the fourth isomorphism above, from which the fifth isomorphism above follows by definition.
The sixth isomorphism above holds because  $k$ is a field of characteristic $0$ (and the groups $H_n$ are finite), and the last isomorphism above is by \cite[Theorem 6.8]{G22}. This completes the proof of the desired lemma.

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $R \stackrel{\sim}{\to} A$ be a semi-free simplicial resolution. Then, the (left) $\Delta H$-module of $n$-simplices in $B_{\rm hOct}(R)$ is of the form $B_{\rm hOct}(F(V))$ for some involutive vector space $V$. It follows from Proposition \ref{pC} that the following natural chain map is a quasi-isomorphism:
 
\begin{equation} \la{srr} k \otimes^{\mathbb{L}}_{\Delta H} {\rm C}(B_{\rm hOct}(R)) \to k \otimes_{\Delta H} {\rm C}(B_{\rm hOct}(R)) \cong {\rm C}(R_{\rm ab, \sigma})\,, \end{equation}
 
where last isomorphism is a consequence of \cite[Theorem 6.8]{G22}. Since \eqref{srr} is precisely the map that induces  $\mathrm{Tr}_{\rm hOct}(A)_\bullet$ on homology, the $\mathrm{Tr}_{\rm hOct}(A)_\bullet$ is an isomorphism of graded $k$-vector spaces.
By Proposition \ref{factorTr}, we then conclude that this isomorphism of vector spaces
is actually an isomorphism of $k$-algebras.

title: Proposition
body_md:
\la{tA}
For any $A \in {\mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_k}^+$, there is an isomorphism of graded $k$-vector spaces $\mathrm{HO}_\bullet(A) \cong \mathrm{HO}_\bullet(N^{\ast}A)$. As a consequence, there is an isomorphism of graded commutative $k$-algebras
 
$${\rm HO}_\bullet(A) \cong \mathrm{HR^{\ob}_{\bullet}}(A,k)\,,$$
 
where $\mathrm{HO}_\bullet(A)$ inherits its algebra structure from $\mathrm{HO}_\bullet(N^*A)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
There are natural quasi-isomorphisms of complexes of $\Delta H$-modules
 
$$B_{\rm hOct}(A) \stackrel{\sim}{\to} B_{\rm hOct} (NN^*A) \stackrel{\sim}{\to} N(B_{\rm hOct} (N^* A))\,, $$
 
where the the first arrow --- induced by the natural weak equivalence $A \to NN^*A$ of DG algebras --- is a weak equivalence by the K\"{u}nneth Theorem, and the second arrow
is a Eilenberg-Zilber map, which is also known to be a quasi-isomorphism by \cite[Sect. A.2]{BRYII}.  Thus, on homology, we get natural isomorphisms of graded $k$-vector spaces
 
$$\mathrm{HO}_\bullet(A):= \mathrm H_\bullet[k \otimes^{\mathbb{L}}_{\Delta H} B_{\rm hOct}(A)] \,\cong\, \mathrm H_\bullet[k \otimes^{\mathbb{L}}_{\Delta H} N(B_{\rm hOct} (N^* A))] =: \mathrm{HO}_\bullet(N^*A)\ . $$
 
proving the first statement in the desired proposition. 

Next, since the functor $(\,\mbox{--}\,)_{\rm ab,\sigma}$ is left adjoint, it commutes with $N^*$: i.e., there is a commutative diagram of functors 
 
\begin{equation} \la{abnst}
\begin{diagram}[small]
{\mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_k}^{+} & \rTo^{N^*} & \mathtt{s}\mathtt{Alg}^{\ob}_k\\
 \dTo^{(\mbox{--})_{\rm ab,\sigma}} & &  \dTo_{(\mbox{--})_{\rm ab,\sigma}}\\
 \mathtt{DGCA}_k^{+} & \rTo^{N^*} & \mathtt{s}\mathtt{CAlg}_k
 \end{diagram}\ .
\end{equation}
 
Let $R \stackrel{\sim}{\to} A$ be a semifree resolution of $A$ in ${\mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_k}^{+}$. There are isomorphisms (that are natural in $R$) 
 
\begin{equation} \la{nnstrh} \mathrm{HR^{\ob}_{\bullet}}(A, k) \,\cong\, \mathrm H_\bullet(R_{\rm ab,\sigma}) \,\cong\, \pi_{\bullet}[N^*(R_{\rm ab,\sigma})] \,\cong\, \pi_\bullet[(N^* R)_{\rm ab,\sigma}]\,\cong\,\mathrm{HR^{\ob}_{\bullet}}(N^*A, k)\ . \end{equation}
 
The first isomorphism above is by definition (see Section \ref{SDRep}), the second isomorphism above is by \eqref{abnst}, and the last isomorphism above is by definition (see Definition \ref{defsrep}) and the fact that $N^*R \to N^*A$ is a semi-free resolution of $A$ (by \cite[Prop. A.2]{BRYII} and since $N^*$ preserves weak-equivalences).  This shows that there is an isomorphism of graded commutative $k$-algebras
 
\begin{equation} \la{hrlnast} \mathrm{HR^{\ob}_{\bullet}}(A,k) \cong \mathrm{HR^{\ob}_{\bullet}}(N^*A, k)\ . \end{equation}
 
The second statement of the desired proposition now follows immediately from Theorem \ref{T1a}.

title: Definition
body_md:
\la{iliealg}
An {\it involution} $\sigma: \mathfrak{a} \to \mathfrak{a}$ is a map of complexes such that $\sigma^2={\rm{Id}}$, and 
$\sigma \circ [\mbox{--},\mbox{--}]\,=\,- [\mbox{--},\mbox{--}] \circ (\sigma \otimes \sigma)\,:\,\mathfrak{a} \otimes \mathfrak{a} \to \mathfrak{a}$. Explicitly, for all $a,b \in \mathfrak{a}$, we have 
$$\sigma([a,b])\,=\,-[\sigma(a), \sigma(b)]\ .$$

title: Remark
body_md:
\la{indinv}
Clearly, if $\sigma$ is an involution on $\mathfrak{a} \in \mathtt{DGL}_k$, then the involution on the tensor algebra $T_k \mathfrak{a} \in \mathtt{DGA}_k$ whose restriction on $\mathfrak{a}$ is $\sigma$ descends to an involution on the universal enveloping algebra $U\mathfrak{a}$ of $\mathfrak{a}$. Thus, $U\mathfrak{a} \in \mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_k$. Abusing notation, we shall continue to denote this notation by $\sigma$.

title: Lemma
body_md:
\la{indinvs}
Let $\mathfrak{a} \in \mathtt{DGL}_k$. Then, the Chevalley-Eilenberg coalgebra ${\mathscr C}(\mathfrak{a};k)$ is a co-commutative skew involutive DG coalgebra. Consequently, the map $\mathbf{\Omega}({\mathscr C}(\mathfrak{a};k)) \stackrel{\sim}{\to} U\mathfrak{a}$ is a (cofibrant) resolution in the category $\mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_{k/k}$ of (augmented) involutive DG $k$-algebras.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
There is a skew involution on the graded (co-commutative) coalgebra ${\mathscr C}(\mathfrak{a};k)$ whose corestriction to $\mathfrak{a}[1]$ is the involution on $\mathfrak{a}$. That this skew involution is compatible with the differential is shown by a direct computation similar to (the proof of) Proposition \ref{skinvtoinv}. It follows that the twisting cochain $\tau: {\mathscr C}(\mathfrak{a};k)[-1] \to \mathfrak{a}$ intertwines the involution on $\mathfrak{a}$ with the skew-involution on ${\mathscr C}(\mathfrak{a};k)$. Consequently, 
$T_k\tau: \mathbf{\Omega}({\mathscr C}(\mathfrak{a};k)) \to T_k\mathfrak{a}$ is a morphism of involutive graded algebras. Since the map $\mathbf{\Omega}({\mathscr C}(\mathfrak{a};k)) \to U\mathfrak{a}$ factors (as a map of graded algebras, forgetting differentials) through the map $T_k\tau$, it is a map of involutive graded algebras. That this map is a quasi-isomorphism of DG algebras is well known (see, e.g., \cite[Theorem 6.1]{BFPRW} and the references therein). Finally $\mathbf{\Omega}(C)$ is cofibrant in $\mathtt{DGA}^{\ob}_{k/k}$ by Theorem \ref{kosdualinv}.

$$
{\rm HO}_\bullet(U\mathfrak{a}) \,\cong\, \left(\Lambda_k[\overline{\mathrm{H}}^{\rm ev}_{\bullet+1}(\mathfrak{a};k)]\right)\,\ .

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\mathfrak{a}=V$ equipped with the trivial Lie bracket. Then, $\mathfrak{a}$ is an involutive Lie algebra, and $U\mathfrak{a} \cong {\rm{Sym}}(V)$ as involutive algebras. ${\mathscr C}(\mathfrak{a};k)=\Lambda_k(V[1])$, with trivial differential and skew involution whose corestriction to $V[1]$ is the involution $\sigma$ on $V$. To compute ${\mathscr C}(\mathfrak{a};k)_+$, we consider its graded $k$-linear dual $E:=\Lambda_k(V^{\ast}[-1])$. This graded commutative $k$-algebra is equipped with a skew involution whose restriction to $V^{\ast}[-1]$ is the operator induced by $\sigma$ on $V^{\ast}$. Abusing notation, denote this skew involution on $E$ by $\sigma$ as well. If $V^\ast_+$ and $V^\ast_-$ denote the $+1$ and $-1$ eigenspaces of $\sigma$ on $V^\ast$ respectively, $E \cong \Lambda(V^{\ast}_+[-1]) \otimes \Lambda(V^{\ast}_-[-1])$. Since $\sigma$ is a skew involution on the graded commutative algebra $E$, 
 
$$\sigma(x_1 \ldots x_n)\,=\,(-1)^{n-1}\sigma(x_1)\ldots \sigma(x_n)\,,\qquad \forall \,x_1,\ldots\,x_n\,\in\,E\ .$$
 
Hence, on the direct summand $\Lambda^i(V^{\ast}_+[-1]) \otimes \Lambda^j(V^{\ast}_-[-1])$ of $E$, $\sigma$ acts by multiplication by $(-1)^{i+j-1}(-1)^j=(-1)^{i-1}$. It follows that the $+1$-eigenspace of the skew involution on $E$ is $\Lambda^{\rm odd}(V^{\ast}_+[-1]) \otimes \Lambda(V^{\ast}_-[-1])$. Dually, ${\mathscr C}(\mathfrak{a};k)_+\,=\,\Lambda^{\rm odd}(V_+[1]) \otimes \Lambda(V_-[1])$. Hence, $\overline{\mathrm{H}}^{\rm ev}_\bullet(\mathfrak{a};k) \,\cong\, \Lambda^{\rm odd}(V_+[1]) \otimes \Lambda(V_-[1])$. The desired lemma now follows from Theorem \ref{houainv}.

title: Proof
body_md:
Abusing notation, let $\sigma$ denote the skew involution on $\mathrm H^{\bullet}(\gl_n(k);k)$ induced by the involution on $\gl_n(k)$. Let $s$ denote the permutation $j \mapsto 2i-j$ in $S_{2i-1}$. Note that ${\rm sgn}(s)=(-1)^{i-1}$. Then, 
\begin{align*}
\sigma\tilde{\omega}_{2i-1}(X_1,\ldots,X_{2i-1}) &= \tilde{\omega}(\sigma(X_1),\ldots,\sigma(X_{2i-1}))\\
 &=\sum_{\tau \in S_{2i-1}} {\rm sgn}(\tau){\rm{Tr}}(\sigma(X_{\tau(1)})\sigma(X_{\tau(2)})\ldots \sigma(X_{\tau(2i-1)}))\\
 &= \sum_{\tau \in S_{2i-1}} {\rm sgn}(\tau){\rm{Tr}}(\sigma(X_{\tau(2i-1)}X_{\tau(2i-2)}\ldots X_{\tau(1)}))\\
 &= \sum_{\tau \in S_{2i-1}} {\rm sgn}(\tau){\rm{Tr}}(X_{\tau(2i-1)}X_{\tau(2i-2)}\ldots X_{\tau(1)})\\
 &= \sum_{\tau \in S_{2i-1}} {\rm sgn}(\tau){\rm{Tr}}(X_{\tau \circ s(1)}X_{\tau \circ s(2)}\ldots X_{\tau \circ s(2i-1)})\\
 &= (-1)^{i-1}\tilde{\omega}(X_1,\ldots,X_{2i-1})\ .
\end{align*}
The fourth equality above is because any involution on $\mathcal{M}_n(k)$ is of the form $X \mapsto J^{-1}X^TJ$ for some $J \in \GL_n(k)$ satisfying $J^T=\pm J$ (see \cite[Thm. 1]{AA}), which implies that any involution on $\mathcal{M}_n(k)$ is trace preserving. Hence, $\sigma(\omega_{4i-3})=\omega_{4i-3}$ and $\sigma(\omega_{4i-1})=-\omega_{4i-1}$ for all $i \geq 1$. As in the proof of Corollary \ref{hosym}, it follows that the $+1$-eigenspace of the induced skew involution on $\mathrm H^{\bullet}(\gl_n(k);k)$ is $\Lambda^{\rm odd}(\omega_1,\omega_5,\ldots,\omega_{4\lfloor \frac{n-1}{4}\rfloor+1}) \otimes \Lambda(\omega_3,\omega_7,\ldots,\omega_{4\lfloor \frac{n-3}{4}\rfloor+3})$. Taking graded linear duals, it follows that 
$$\overline{\mathrm{H}}^{\rm ev}_{\bullet}(\gl_n(k);k) \,\cong\, \Lambda^{\rm odd}(\xi_1,\xi_5,\ldots,\xi_{4\lfloor \frac{n-1}{4}\rfloor+1}) \otimes \Lambda(\xi_3,\xi_7,\ldots,\xi_{4\lfloor \frac{n-3}{4}\rfloor+3})\ .$$ The desired formula for ${\rm HO}_\bullet(U\gl_n(k))$ then follows immediately from Theorem \ref{houainv}. The proof of the formula for ${\rm HO}_\bullet(U\mathfrak{sl}_n(k))$ is identical but for one minor modification: the (co)generators $\omega_1$ and $\xi_1$ are omitted.

title: Proposition
body_md:
\la{grcomp}
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$ and $\Gamma \in \sGr$ a simplicial group. Then there is a natural isomorphism $\,\mathrm{HR^{\ob}_{\bullet}}(k[\Gamma], k^n) \cong {\rm HR}_\bullet(\Gamma, \GLm)$. In particular, $\mathrm{HR^{\ob}_{\bullet}}(k[\Gamma], k) \cong {\rm HR}_\bullet(\Gamma, \mtwo)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The proof follows that of \cite[Theorem 2.1]{BR22c}, with the category $\fM$ of finitely generated free monoids replaced by the category $\fM^{\sigma}$ of finitely generated free involutive monoids $\langle m \rangle^\sigma := J\big((C_2 \times \underline{m})_+\big)$ (the free monoid on the free $C_2$-set with $m$ orbits $\{x_i, \bar{x}_i\}$, with involution induced by the $C_2$-action), and $p: \fM^\sigma \to \fG$ the group completion functor, $\bar{x}_i \mapsto x_i^{-1}$. First, for any simplicial involutive monoid $N$, one has 
 
\begin{equation} \la{torhr}  {\rm Tor}^{\fM^\sigma}_\bullet(k[N], \underline{\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{M}_n)}) \cong \mathrm{HR^{\ob}_{\bullet}}(k[N], k^n)\,,\end{equation}
 
where $\underline{\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{M}_n)}$ is the left $\fM^{\sigma}$-module given by $\underline{\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{M}_n)}(\langle m \rangle^\sigma) := (k\langle m\rangle^\sigma)^{\ob}_n = \mathcal{O}(\mathcal{M}_n^{\,m})$. The isomorphism \eqref{torhr} is analogous to \cite[Proposition 2.1]{BR22c}, whose proof goes through in the involutive setting with the obvious modifications using a semi-free resolution $R \,\stackrel{\sim}{\twoheadrightarrow}\, N$ in the category if simplicial involutive algebras. 
Next, note that there is an isomorphism in the derived category of $\fG$-modules
 
\begin{equation} \la{lpsho} \mathbb{L} p_!\,\underline{\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{M}_n)} \cong \underline{\mathcal{O}(\GLm)}\ .\end{equation}
 
Indeed, since $k\langle m \rangle$ is a projective right $\fG$-module and by \cite[Lemma 2.1]{BR22c},
 
$$ \mathbb{L} p_!\,\underline{\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{M}_n)}(\langle m \rangle)\,\cong\, k[\langle m\rangle] \otimes^{\mathbb{L}}_{\fG} \mathbb{L} p_! \,\underline{\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{M}_n)}\,\cong\, p^\ast k[\langle m \rangle] \otimes^{\mathbb{L}}_{\fM^{\sigma}} \underline{\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{M}_n)}\ .$$
 
By \eqref{torhr},
 
$$\mathrm H_\bullet[p^\ast k[\langle m \rangle] \otimes^{\mathbb{L}}_{\fM^{\sigma}} \underline{\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{M}_n)}]\,\cong\, \mathrm{HR^{\ob}_{\bullet}}(k[\langle m\rangle], k^n)\ .$$
 
Verifying \eqref{lpsho} then amounts to the vanishing of ${\rm HR}^{\ast}_i(k[\langle m\rangle ], k^n)$ for all $i > 0$ and ${\rm HR}^{\ast}_0(k[\langle m \rangle], k^n) = \mathcal{O}\big((\GLm)^m\big)$. This is \cite[Theorem 1.7]{BR14} applied to $A = k[\langle m \rangle]$, which is formally smooth and admits a semi-free involutive resolution that is finitely finitely generated in each degree (also see Remark \ref{grrational} and Example \ref{grex} (4) below for a different proof of this vanishing for $n=1$). Finally, 
 
$$ {\rm HR}_\bullet(\Gamma, \GLm):={\rm Tor}^{\fG}_\bullet(k[\Gamma], \underline{\mathcal{O}(\GLm)})\cong{\rm Tor}^{\fG}_\bullet(k[\Gamma], \mathbb{L} p_!\,\underline{\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{M}_n)})\cong {\rm Tor}^{\fM^{\sigma}}_\bullet(k[\Gamma], \underline{\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{M}_n)})\cong \mathrm{HR^{\ob}_{\bullet}}(k[\Gamma],k^n)\ . $$
The second isomorphism above is by \eqref{lpsho}, the third isomorphism is by \cite[Lemma 2.1]{BR22c} and the last isomorphism is by \eqref{torhr}. This proves the desired proposition.

title: Lemma
body_md:
\la{grPsidih}
The functor $\Psicyc$ extends to a functor $\Psidih: \Delta D \to \fG$, $[n] \mapsto \langle n+1\rangle$, by
 
$$ \Psidih(r_n):\ \langle n+1 \rangle \to \langle n+1 \rangle\,,\qquad (x_0, x_1, \ldots, x_n) \mapsto (x_0^{-1}, x_n^{-1}, \ldots, x_1^{-1})\ . $$
 
For a discrete group $\Gamma$, $\Psidih^\ast(\underline{\Gamma}): \Delta D^{\rm op} \to \mathtt{Sets}$ is the dihedral bar construction of $\Gamma$, $\,r_n(g_0, \ldots, g_n) = (g_0^{-1}, g_n^{-1}, \ldots, g_1^{-1})$, so that $k[\Psidih^\ast\underline{\Gamma}] = B^{\rm dih}(k[\Gamma])$ is the dihedral bar construction of the involutive algebra $k[\Gamma]$ of Section~\ref{bardihhoct}.

body_md: The dihedral relations $r_n t_n = t_n^{-1} r_n$, $r_n^2 = 1$, $r_n d_i = d_{n-i} r_{n-1}$ and $r_n s_j = s_{n-j} r_{n+1}$ (in $\Delta D$) are verified on the free groups $\langle n+1 \rangle$ by direct substitution, exactly as the cyclic relations in \cite[Lemma 3.10]{BR22}. title: Lemma
body_md:
\la{grinv}
For an affine group scheme $G$ over $k$,
 
$$ \Hom_{{\rm Mod}_k(\Delta D)}\big(k, B_{\rm dih}\mathcal{O}(G)\big)\,\cong\,\mathcal{O}(G)^{G,\iota}\,:=\,\{P \in \mathcal{O}(G)^G\,:\, P(g^{-1}) = P(g)\}\,, $$
 
the algebra of conjugation invariant functions on $G$ that are also invariant under inversion.

title: Proof
body_md:
By \cite[Lemma 3.14]{BR22}, there is an isomorphism $\Hom_{{\rm Mod}_k(\Delta C)}(k, B_{\rm cyc}\mathcal{O}(G)) \cong \mathcal{O}(G)^G$, with an invariant $P$ corresponding to the family $(\Delta_G^{(m)}P)_{m \geq 0}$, where $\Delta_G^{(m)}P(g_0, \ldots, g_m) = P(g_0 \cdots g_m)$. The naturality with respect to the additional generators $r_m$ of $\Delta D$ reads  $\,\Delta^{(m)}_GP \circ \Psidih(r_m) = \Delta^{(m)}_GP\,$, which is
explicitly the following condition
 
\begin{equation} \la{invpg} P(g_0^{-1}g_m^{-1}\cdots g_1^{-1}) = P(g_0 \cdots g_m) \end{equation} 
 
for all $g_i \in G$. For $m=0$, this yields $P(g^{-1}) = P(g)$ for all $g \in G$. Conversely, the condition $P(g^{-1}) = P(g)$ for all $g \in G$ together with conjugation invariance implies the condition \eqref{invpg} for all $m$, since $g_0^{-1}g_m^{-1}\cdots g_1^{-1} = (g_1 \cdots g_m g_0)^{-1}$ is conjugate to $(g_0 \cdots g_m)^{-1}$.

title: Proof
body_md:
The isomorphism \eqref{HRDA} follows from \eqref{XAeq} and \eqref{HXA}, using the fact that a simplicial abelian group is a product of Eilenberg-MacLane spaces and that $\pi_i\,\Omega\,\SPi(X;{\mathcal A}) = \tilde{\mathrm H}_{i+1}(X;{\mathcal A})$. To prove \eqref{XAeq}, we follow the proof of \cite[Theorem 4.2]{BR22}.

First, we assume that  ${\mathcal A} = R$ is the additive group of a commutative ring $R$. Since the functor $\Gamma \mapsto \Gamma_{\rm ab} \otimes_\mathbb{Z} R$ from groups to $R$-modules is left adjoint to the forgetful functor, its degreewise extension $(\,\mbox{--}\,)_{{\rm ab},R}: \sGr \to \mathtt{s}{\rm Mod}_R$ is a left Quillen functor (as the right adjoint does not change the underlying simplicial sets). By \eqref{Shapiro},
 
\begin{equation} \la{hcl1} \hocolim_{\fG_R^{\rm op}} (p^\ast\Gamma) \simeq \int_{\mathbb{L}}^{\langle n \rangle \in \fG}\Gamma\langle n\rangle \times R^n\ .\end{equation} 
 
Next, the bifunctor $\Gamma \times F_R: \fG^{\rm op}\times \fG \to \sSet$ factors as 
 
$$ 
\fG^{\rm op}\times\fG \xrightarrow{\Gamma \otimes \mathbb{F}} \sGr \xrightarrow{(\mbox{--})_{{\rm ab},R}} \mathtt{s}{\rm Mod}_R \to \sSet
$$
 
where $\Gamma \otimes \mathbb{F}$ is the objectwise cofibrant bifunctor of \cite[(4-16)]{BR22}. Since derived left Quillen functors commute with homotopy coends (see \cite[(2-20)]{BR22}),
 
\begin{equation} \la{hcl2} \mathbb{L}[\mathbb{L} K(\Gamma)]_{{\rm ab},R} \simeq \int_L^{\langle n \rangle \in \fG} \mathbb{L}(\Gamma\langle n\rangle \otimes \mathbb{F}\langle n \rangle)_{{\rm ab},R} \simeq \int_L^{\langle n \rangle \in \fG}(\Gamma\langle n\rangle \otimes \mathbb{F}\langle n \rangle)_{{\rm ab},R} \simeq \int_{\mathbb{L}}^{\langle n \rangle \in \fG}\Gamma\langle n\rangle \times R^n  \end{equation}
 
where $\mathbb{L} K(\Gamma)$ is the simplicial group associated to $\Gamma$ by \cite[Theorem 3.2]{BR22}. The first weak equivalence above uses \cite[(3-11)]{BR22} and the second is because $\Gamma \otimes \mathbb{F}$ is objectwise cofibrant. On the other hand,
$$\mathbb{L}[\mathbb{L} K(\Gamma)]_{{\rm ab},R} \simeq [\mathbb{G}\overline{W} \mathbb{L} K(\Gamma)]_{{\rm ab},R} \simeq \mathbb{A}(\overline{W} \mathbb{L} K(\Gamma))\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}} R\,, $$
since the Kan loop group $\mathbb{G}\overline{W} \mathbb{L} K(\Gamma)$ is cofibrant and weakly-equivalent to $\mathbb{L} K(\Gamma)$. Therefore, 
 
\begin{equation} \la{hcl3} \hocolim_{\fG_R^{\rm op}} p^\ast\Gamma \simeq \mathbb{A}(X) \otimes R \end{equation}
 
where $X := \overline{W}\mathbb{L} K(\Gamma) \simeq B\Gamma$.  Note that the weak-equivalence \eqref{hurw} between levelwise free simplicial abelian groups remains a weak-equivalence after $\otimes_\mathbb{Z} R$. Further, by the very definition of $\overline{W}$,  $\overline{W}\mathbb{A}(X)\otimes R = \overline{W}(\mathbb{A}(X)\otimes R)$. Since, in addition,  $|V| \simeq \Omega|\overline{W}V|$ for any simplicial group $V$, we conclude
 
$$ |\mathbb{A}(X)\otimes R|\,\simeq\,\Omega\,|\bar{W}(\mathbb{A}(X)\otimes R)|\,\simeq\,\Omega\,|\widetilde{\mathbb{Z}}[X]\otimes R|\,=\,\Omega\,\SPi(X;R)\,, $$
 
naturally in $X$. This proves \eqref{XAeq} for ${\mathcal A} = R$.

Now, if ${\mathcal A}$ is finitely generated, then ${\mathcal A} \cong \mathbb{Z}^r \oplus \bigoplus_i \mathbb{Z}/m_i$ is the additive group of the commutative ring $\mathbb{Z}^r \times \prod_i \mathbb{Z}/m_i$, hence the above argument applies, proving \eqref{XAeq} for finitely generated abelian groups.

Finally, for an arbitrary abelian group ${\mathcal A}$, we write ${\mathcal A} = \varinjlim {\mathcal A}_\alpha$ as the filtered colimit of its finitely generated subgroups. Both sides of \eqref{XAeq} commute with filtered colimits in ${\mathcal A}$: $F_{{\mathcal A}} = \varinjlim F_{{{\mathcal A}}_\alpha}$, homotopy colimits commute with filtered colimits, $\mathbb{A}(X)\otimes {\mathcal A} = \varinjlim \mathbb{A}(X)\otimes {\mathcal A}_\alpha$, and geometric realization commutes with filtered colimits. Naturality in $\Gamma$ is clear at every step. This proves \eqref{XAeq} in general. \eqref{HRDA} follows immediately from \eqref{XAeq}.

For the last assertion, note that $K(V, j)$ is rationally trivial for $j \geq 1$ when $V$ is a torsion group, while $\pi_0\,\Omega\,\SPi(B\Gamma;{\mathcal A}) = \mathrm H_1(B\Gamma;{\mathcal A}) = \pi_0(\Gamma)_{\rm ab} \otimes {\mathcal A}$.

For any $\Gamma \in \sGrh$ and any commutative ring $k$, 
$${\rm HR}_\bullet(\Gamma, \mtwo) \cong \mathrm H_\bullet\big(\Omega\,\SPi(B\Gamma;\mathbb{Z}/2);k\big)\ .$$ 
If $k \supseteq \mathbb{Q}$, then 
$${\rm HR}_\bullet(\Gamma,\mtwo) \cong k[\mathrm H_1(B\Gamma;\mathbb{Z}/2)] = k[\pi_0(\Gamma)_{\rm ab}\otimes \mathbb{Z}/2]\,,$$ 
concentrated in degree $0$. If $k = \mathbb{F}_2$, then ${\rm HR}_\bullet(\Gamma,\mtwo)$ is the mod $2$ homology of the generalized Eilenberg-MacLane space $\prod_{i \geq 1}K(\tilde{\mathrm H}_i(B\Gamma;\mathbb{F}_2), i-1)$.

title: Remark
body_md:
\la{grm2}
Theorem~\ref{Tgroups} is a statement about representation homology alone, valid for every abelian group ${\mathcal A}$. What is special about ${\mathcal A} = \mathbb{Z}/2$ is the existence of the dihedral/hyperoctahedral factorization of Section~\ref{Sgr6}: for $m \geq 3$, $\mu_m = \ker(g \mapsto g^m)$ is not the fixed point scheme of any (anti-)automorphism of $\mathbb{G}_m$, there is no involution on $k[\Gamma]$ with $(k[\Gamma])^{\ob}_1 = k[\Gamma_{\rm ab}\otimes\mathbb{Z}/m]$, and the lifting problem of Proposition~\ref{grlift} below has no solution modulo $m$. For general $m$, one only has the composite of the map of \cite[Proposition 4.8]{BR22} with the map induced on representation homology by the inclusion $\mu_m \to \mathbb{G}_m$ of coefficients, ${\rm HS}_\bullet(k[\Gamma]) \to {\rm HR}_\bullet(\Gamma,\mathbb{G}_m) \to {\rm HR}_\bullet(\Gamma, \mu_m)$, realized by 
$$ \Omega\,\Omega^\infty\Sigma^\infty(B\Gamma) \to \Omega\,\SPi(B\Gamma) \to \Omega\,\SPi(B\Gamma;\mathbb{Z}/m)
$$

title: Lemma
body_md:
\la{grPsihyp}
The functor $\Psisym$ extends to a functor 
$$\Psihyp: \Delta H \to \fG^{\rm op}\,, \qquad [n] \mapsto \langle n+1\rangle\, $$ sending $f = X_0 \otimes \cdots \otimes X_m$ to the homomorphism $\langle m+1 \rangle \to \langle n+1 \rangle$ given by 
 
$$ \Psihyp(f):\ (x_j \in \langle m+1 \rangle) \mapsto (x_{i_1}^{\epsilon_{i_1}} \cdots x_{i_r}^{\epsilon_{i_r}} \in \langle n+1\rangle)\quad\text{if}\quad X_j = x_{i_1}^{\alpha_{i_1}}\cdots x_{i_r}^{\alpha_{i_r}}\,,$$
 
where $\epsilon_i= \pm 1$ depending on whether $\alpha_i=1$ ot $\alpha_i=s$. 
There is a commutative diagram of functors 
 
$$
\begin{diagram}[small]
\Delta C^{\rm op} & \rTo^{i} & \Delta S & \rTo^{\Psi_{\rm sym}} & \fG^{\rm op}\\
 \dInto & & \dInto & &  \dTo^{\rm Id}\\
\Delta D^{\rm op}  & \rTo^{i} & \Delta H & \rTo^{\Psi_{\rm hOct}} & \fG^{\rm op}\\
\end{diagram}
$$
 
where the first two vertical arrows are the obvious inclusions, the functor $i:\Delta D^{\rm op} \to \Delta H$ is the inclusion defined in \cite[3.3]{G21}, and the functor $i:\Delta C^{\rm op} \to \Delta S$ is the inclusion defined in \cite[6.1.11]{L}. For a discrete group $\Gamma$, $\Psihyp^\ast(\underline{\Gamma})$ is the hyperoctahedral bar construction of the group $\Gamma$ with $\bar{g} = g^{-1}$ \cite[Definition 7.12]{G21}, so that $k[\Psihyp^\ast\underline{\Gamma}] = B_{\rm hOct}(k[\Gamma])$.

body_md: Composition in $\Delta H$ is substitution of monomials, with the reversal rule for $(\,\mbox{--}\,)^s$ recalled above: under $x_i^s = x_i^{-1}$ this rule becomes the identity $(x_{i_1}^{\epsilon_{i_1}}\cdots x_{i_r}^{\epsilon_{i_r}})^{-1} = x_{i_r}^{-\epsilon_{i_r}}\cdots x_{i_1}^{-\epsilon_{i_1}}$ in the free group. The commutativity of the square and the last statement are immediate from the definitions (cf. \cite[Lemma 4.3]{BR22} and \cite[Definition 7.12]{G21}).

title: Proof
body_md:
For $f \in \Hom_{\Delta H}([n], [m])$ in tensor notation, the abelianization $\Psihyp(f)_{\rm ab}: \mathbb{Z}^{m+1} \to \mathbb{Z}^{n+1}$ is given by (left multiplication by) the integral $(n+1) \times (m+1)$-matrix whose $j$-th column has entries $\epsilon_i = 1$ in the rows $i$ with $x_i$ occurring in $X_j$, $\epsilon_i=-1$ in the rows with $x_i^s$ occurring in $X_j$ and $0$ elsewhere. Since for each $i$, exactly one of the pair $\{x_i,x_i^s\}$ occurs exactly once among the $X_0,\ldots,X_m$, every row contains exactly one nonzero entry, equal to $\pm 1$. Hence $\Psihyp(f)_{\rm ab}$ maps $(1, \ldots, 1)$ to $(\pm 1, \ldots, \pm 1)$, which is $(\bar{1}, \ldots, \bar{1})$ modulo $2$. This shows that \eqref{tPsihyp} is a well-defined functor lifting $\Psihyp$ through $p^{\rm op}: \fG_{\mathbb{Z}/2}^{\rm op} \to \fG^{\rm op}$, and that 
 
$$ k[B_{\rm hOct}\Gamma] = \Psihyp^\ast k[\Gamma] = \tPsihyp^\ast(k[p^\ast\Gamma])\ .$$ 
By \cite[Lemma 3.13]{BR22}, $\tPsihyp$ induces a map 
$$\mathrm{HO}_\bullet(k[\Gamma]) \to {\rm Tor}^{\fG_{\mathbb{Z}/2}^{\rm op}}_\bullet(k, k[p^\ast\Gamma])\,\cong \, {\rm HR}_\bullet(\Gamma,\mtwo)\,,$$ where the last isomorphism is  by \eqref{Shapiro}. The factorization ${\rm{Tr}}^\sigma(\Gamma)_\bullet = \tPsihyp^\ast\circ i^\ast$ is verified exactly as in \cite[Proposition 4.8]{BR22}: with a projective resolution $Q \,\stackrel{\sim}{\twoheadrightarrow}\, k[\Gamma]$, the Shapiro isomorphism is represented by \cite[(4-37)]{BR22} with $\mathbb{Z}^n$ replaced by $(\mathbb{Z}/2)^n$, and the composite $\tPsihyp^\ast\circ i^\ast$ by \cite[(4-38)]{BR22} with $(\langle m+1\rangle; 1, \ldots, 1)$ replaced by $(\langle m+1 \rangle; \bar{1}, \ldots, \bar{1})$: the resulting map $v_{m+1} \mapsto v_{m+1}\otimes[(\bar{1},\ldots,\bar{1})]$ is \eqref{grTr}.

title: Proof
body_md: Assume first that $\Gamma$ is a simplicial group. By Theorem~\ref{T1a} applied to the simplicial involutive algebra $k[\Gamma]$, $\mathrm{Tr}_{\rm hOct}(k[\Gamma])_\bullet: \mathrm{HO}_\bullet(k[\Gamma]) \to \mathrm{HR^{\ob}_{\bullet}}(k[\Gamma], k)$ is an isomorphism of graded commutative algebras, and by Proposition~\ref{grcomp}, $\mathrm{HR^{\ob}_{\bullet}}(k[\Gamma], k) \cong {\rm HR}_\bullet(\Gamma,\mtwo)$. One checks, as in the proof of \cite[Corollary 3.1]{BR22c}, that the composite of these two isomorphisms is $\tPsihyp^\ast$: both maps are induced by the augmentation $k\otimes^{\mathbb{L}}_{\Delta H} \to k \otimes_{\Delta H}$ followed by the Shapiro identification. Note that $\sGrh$ reduces to $\sGr$ by Badzioch's theorem \cite[Theorem 3.2]{BR22} and homotopy invariance. The last assertion is Corollary~\ref{grchar0}.

title: Remark
body_md:
\la{grrational}
For a discrete group $\Gamma$, the isomorphism $\tPsihyp^\ast$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ can also be seen directly on the spaces of Corollary~\ref{grspaces}, without using Proposition~\ref{grcomp}. The map $\tPsihyp$ in \eqref{grmaps} is induced by the natural transformation of functors on based $C_2$-sets
 
$$ C_\infty\big(EC_{2+}\wedge_{C_2}X\big) \longrightarrow \SPi\big(X/C_2\big) = \mathbb{N}\big[(X\smallsetminus\ast)/C_2\big]\,, $$
 
composed of the map of monads $C_\infty \to \SPi$ (from $E_\infty$ to commutative monoids) and the collapse $EC_2 \to {\rm pt}$, applied inside the bar construction; the target is $B\big(\SPi\circ(\,\mbox{--}\,/C_2), C_1, \Gamma\big) = |B(J, J, \Gamma)_{{\rm ab},\sigma}|$, the derived involutive abelianization of the monoid $\Gamma$ (the involutive counterpart of \cite[Proposition 4.11]{BR22}). By the Cartan-Leray theorem, $\mathrm H_\bullet\big(C_\infty(EC_{2+}\wedge_{C_2}X);\mathbb{Q}\big) \cong {\rm{Sym}}\big(\mathbb{Q}[(X\smallsetminus\ast)/C_2]\big)$ for a discrete based $C_2$-set $X$ (cf. the proof of Proposition~\ref{pC}), so the map is a rational homology isomorphism levelwise in the bar construction, and hence on realizations.

body_md: For $n > 1$ and $G = \GLm$ (an orthogonal or symplectic group), Example~\ref{grtraces}$(2)$ gives dihedral character maps ${\rm{Tr}}^\sigma_n(\Gamma)_\bullet: \mathrm{HD}_\bullet(k[\Gamma]) \to {\rm HR}_\bullet(\Gamma,\GLm)^{\GLm}$, which assemble into a map of graded commutative algebras $\Lambda{\rm{Tr}}^\sigma_n: \Lambda_k[\overline{\mathrm{HD}}_\bullet(k[\Gamma])] \to {\rm HR}_\bullet(\Gamma,\GLm)^{\GLm}$. In can be shown, in analogy with \cite[Theorem 1.4]{BR22} (also see \cite[Sec. 8.5]{BFPRW}), that $\Lambda{\rm{Tr}}^\sigma_\infty$ becomes an isomorphism in the stable range $n \to \infty$ for $B\Gamma$ simply connected of finite rational type --- a derived (Koszul dual) form of the Loday-Procesi theorem expressing the homology of $\mathfrak{o}_\infty(A)$ and $\mathfrak{sp}_\infty(A)$ in terms of dihedral homology. We do not pursue this here.
